title: The Source That Could Not Be Cited
story: The seminar required a footnote for every claim, yet Samir's best source sat in a private archive that forbade quotation. He could paraphrase the argument in his own words, but he could not point a reader to the page. His partner wanted the claim removed, because an uncheckable sentence looked like ornament. Samir wanted it kept, because removal would make the essay neater and less true. The tutor allowed the sentence only beside a note that the source could not be consulted. She marked the paper on whether that limit was shown honestly. A hidden advantage, she said, was worse than a visible gap.

vocabulary.definition: A note telling a reader where a claim comes from
A store of records that is not open to everyone
To retell an idea in your own words
Decoration that adds little real substance
Looked at in order to check something
A benefit that puts someone in a stronger position

quiz.question: On what condition could Samir's sentence stay?
options: Beside a note that the source could not be consulted
Only if his partner signed every footnote
Only after the archive lifted its ban
Only once the claim had been deleted
quiz.correctAnswer: Beside a note that the source could not be consulted
quiz.explanation: The tutor allowed the sentence only beside a note that the source could not be consulted.
quiz.supportingSentence: The tutor allowed the sentence only beside a note that the source could not be consulted.

quiz.question: What did the partner want done with the uncheckable claim?
options: Removed from the essay
Printed as a long quotation
Moved into another seminar
Checked against a public copy
quiz.explanation: The partner wanted the claim removed.
quiz.supportingSentence: His partner wanted the claim removed, because an uncheckable sentence looked like ornament.

quiz.question: What did Samir think a neater essay would lose?
options: Part of what was true
His partner's name on the cover
Entry to the private archive
Every footnote in the seminar
quiz.explanation: He believed removal would make the essay neater and less true.
quiz.supportingSentence: Samir wanted it kept, because removal would make the essay neater and less true.

quiz.question: What does paraphrase mean in Samir's case?
options: Saying the idea in his own words
Copying an archive page in full
Deleting the sentence before marking
Asking the tutor to invent a source
quiz.correctAnswer: Saying the idea in his own words
quiz.explanation: Paraphrase is paired with retelling the argument in his own words.
quiz.supportingSentence: He could paraphrase the argument in his own words, but he could not point a reader to the page.

quiz.question: Why does the passage end by ranking a hidden advantage against a visible gap?
options: To state the standard she would mark by
To admit the archive ban had been lifted
To show the partner changed his mind
To list claims that needed no footnote
quiz.correctAnswer: To state the standard she would mark by
quiz.explanation: The closing comparison is the standard behind marking the paper for honesty.
quiz.supportingSentence: A hidden advantage, she said, was worse than a visible gap.
